# Commit hooks exec a hard-coded per-user path → `git worktree add` and `wl sync` fail

## Problem statement

The committed hooks `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge` and
`.githooks/post-rewrite` unconditionally `exec` the absolute path
`/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. That path is
per-user and machine-specific, so on any host where it is absent (a different
username, a clean machine, CI) every checkout, merge and `git worktree add` in
this repository exits 127 — which in turn breaks `wl sync` (its
temporary-worktree merge) and `implement.py start`/`finish` worktree creation.
The repository already commits the real script as `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`,
but no wrapper references it.

## Reproduction

```sh
cd /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents
# The wrapper hard-codes an absolute path, so the failure is independent of
# $HOME. Simulate a host where that path does not exist by moving the central
# symlink aside for one command (restore it afterwards):
LINK=$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull
mv "$LINK" "$LINK.bak"
git worktree add --detach /tmp/sa-wt-repro HEAD
mv "$LINK.bak" "$LINK"
# → .githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
# → rc=127 (verified during intake)
```

On the current agent host the immediate trigger is masked because
`/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` exists as a symlink to
this repo's committed script (installed by `scripts/install_pi.sh`), so normal
runs here exit 0 ("worklog: sync failed or not initialized; continuing"). The
defect is therefore latent on this host and reproduces on every host or clean
clone where that absolute path is absent.

## Users

- **AI agent driving `/skill:implement`** — needs `implement.py start`/`finish`
  to create worktrees without a hook failure aborting the run.
  Story: *As an implementing agent, when I start work on an item, the worktree
  is created successfully even though the machine has no central hook install.*
- **Agent or developer running `wl sync`** — needs the sync push to complete.
  Story: *As an agent publishing Worklog data, `wl sync` completes its push
  step on a clean clone without setting `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` or
  `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`.*
- **Developer on a second machine / CI checkout** — needs the committed hooks
  to be portable.
  Story: *As a developer whose username is not `rgardler`, cloning and
  checking out this repository does not emit `exec: ... not found`.*
- **Framework maintainer** — needs the behaviour pinned by a regression test.
  Story: *As a maintainer of the agent framework, I need a test that fails if a
  committed hook regains a hard-coded per-user path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **No hard-coded per-user path.** The three wrappers
      (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite`) resolve the
      post-pull script without any absolute `/home/<user>` path: they first try
      the repository-relative `<toplevel>/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, then
      `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, and when neither exists
      they print one clear line to stderr and exit 0 (never 127, never a silent
      failure).
- [ ] **Regression test proving `git worktree add` succeeds.** A hermetic test
      asserts (a) the committed wrappers contain no absolute `/home/<user>` or
      other machine-specific path; (b) in a temp repository built from the
      committed `.githooks/` with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a sandboxed
      `$HOME` that has no `.config/pi`, and a stubbed `wl` on `PATH`,
      `git worktree add --detach <tmp> HEAD` exits 0, emits no
      `exec: ... not found`, and reaches the repo-relative
      `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`; and (c) the same setup with
      `worklog-post-pull` absent takes the graceful no-op path (one stderr
      notice naming the attempted locations, `rc=0`, no sync attempted).
- [ ] **`wl sync` completes its push step** in this repository on a host
      without the central hook install (sandboxed `$HOME`), without the
      `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` / `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` workaround.
- [ ] **Hooks cannot recurse.** A hook-triggered sync from `wl`'s own
      `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (and from a linked worktree) exits before
      calling `wl sync`, matching the guards already present in the sibling
      ContextHub/AI_Hell hooks.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries —
      specifically replacing the portability caveat in `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`
      and updating the `install_pi.sh` fail-open warning to match the new hook
      behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Hooks are POSIX `sh` executed by git; they must stay dependency-free (no
  python, no network) and fast, because they run on every checkout/merge.
- `$HOME` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` must both be treated as
  best-effort: hook execution inherits git's environment, and earlier incidents
  (SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K, SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8) showed `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*` pollution
  in spawned sessions. Every resolution step fails open.
- Keep the shared-script model (one implementation in
  `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`) rather than inlining a copy into each wrapper;
  the sibling repositories' self-contained hooks are precedent for the guards,
  not for duplicating sync logic.
- Do not touch the `pre-push` hook behaviour (`worklog:pre-push-hook:v3`) or the
  full-suite gate; this item changes only the post-pull chain.
- Sibling project checkouts (`ContentCreator`, `ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) are out
  of scope; the ContextHub/AI_Hell copies are reference implementations only,
  and any divergence found there becomes a linked follow-up item.
- Build → test → commit order; no ad-hoc `pytest` — use the test skill /
  `run_tests.py`.
- Preserve the existing bypass variables (`WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1`,
  `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1`) and their documented semantics.

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- The three wrappers are 184-byte files with header
  `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1` and a single
  `exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"` line
  (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite`).
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` **is committed** (514 bytes; runs `wl sync`,
  honours `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1`, fail-open when `wl` is absent). Nothing
  in the repository invokes it: `rg worklog-post-pull` finds only the wrappers'
  hard-coded path, `scripts/install_pi.sh` (central install), one test file and
  the docs.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs the central script as an executable symlink
  to the repo copy (`create_symlink`, idempotent, `PI_SKIP_HOOK_INSTALL=1`
  gated) and then emits a **warning only** when a project's committed wrapper
  does not reference that central path. The warning does not fix the wrapper.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` (~lines 100–120) documents the delegation and
  carries a "Portability caveat (SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX)" paragraph describing
  exactly this defect as unresolved.
- Sibling repositories (`ContextHub`, `AI_Hell`) ship
  self-contained `post-checkout`/`worklog-post-pull` hooks that (a) skip
  `*tmp-worktree-*` paths and (b) skip linked worktrees
  (`git rev-parse --git-dir` vs `--git-common-dir`). The SorraAgents copy of
  `worklog-post-pull` lacks both guards. (`ContentCreator` is reported in the
  consolidated duplicate item to have the same self-contained pattern, but that
  checkout is not present on this host, so it was not verified directly.)
- Verified on this host: `git worktree add --detach /tmp/sa-wt-intake-check HEAD`
  now exits 0 ("worklog: sync failed or not initialized; continuing") because
  the central symlink exists — the hard-coded path is what breaks elsewhere.
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` covers the *installer* and writes
  its own synthetic hooks; no test asserts the content or behaviour of this
  repository's committed wrappers.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` and `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`
  cover the pre-push wiring only.

## Desired change

1. Rewrite the three wrappers to resolve the post-pull script in this order:
   repository-relative (via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, falling back to
   `dirname "$0"`), then `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, then a
   single-line stderr notice + `exit 0`. No literal `/home/<user>` anywhere.
2. Add the `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards to
   `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` so a hook-triggered sync cannot nest inside
   `wl sync`'s own temporary worktree, mirroring the sibling implementations.
3. Update the `install_pi.sh` portability warning to reflect the fixed
   behaviour (warning remains a guard for *forked/older* wrappers only).
4. Replace the docs caveat with the actual resolution order and the no-op
   behaviour; document the bypass variables.
5. Add the hermetic regression test described in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite` — replace the hard-coded `exec` with portable resolution + graceful no-op.
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — add tmp-worktree and linked-worktree guards; keep `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL` bypass.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — adjust the fail-open portability warning/message to the new contract.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — replace the portability caveat with the resolution order and no-op semantics.
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` — new hermetic regression tests (worktree add succeeds under a sandboxed `$HOME`; no-op path; bypass; no hard-coded `/home/<user>` in committed hooks).
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` — extend only if the installer warning contract changes.

## Related work

- `SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` — *Chore: install central wl post-pull hook
  (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing* (completed): installed the
  central symlink and the wrapper-to-central delegation this item now makes
  portable.
- `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` — *SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing
  central script* (closed as duplicate of this item; its reproduction
  transcript, sibling self-contained-hook precedent and `WORKLOG_SKIP_*`
  behaviour are folded in above).
- `SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM` — *install_pi.sh propagates the SorraAgents-only test
  gate to non-SorraAgents projects* (completed): precedent for project-vs-framework
  hook variants in the same installer block.
- `SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K`, `SA-0MUIZSXEY008NGR8` — hook/GIT environment
  investigations that motivate fail-open resolution.
- `SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX` — pre-push git-identity guard (same hook family; do not
  regress it).
- Related docs: `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.
- Related files: `.githooks/pre-push` (v3 pattern for `git rev-parse`-based
  resolution), sibling `.githooks/{post-checkout,worklog-post-pull}` in
  `ContextHub`/`AI_Hell`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** repo-relative resolution is the intended shape (the ACs allow
  either repo-relative delegation or inline logic; the repository already
  commits `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, so reusing it is the minimal change).
- **Assumption:** keeping `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` as a
  second candidate preserves compatibility with framework projects whose
  wrappers are installed by `install_pi.sh`.
- **Risk:** `git rev-parse` inside a hook can be misled by `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_*`
  pollution. Mitigation: `2>/dev/null`, fall back to `dirname "$0"`, then
  `$HOME`, then no-op.
- **Risk:** a no-op can hide a broken install. Mitigation: the stderr line names
  both attempted paths and points at `scripts/install_pi.sh`.
- **Risk:** the new test could invoke real `wl` (network/sync side effects).
  Mitigation: sandboxed `$HOME`, stub `wl` on `PATH`, or assert the no-op path
  only; never perform a real sync in the test.
- **Scope-creep risk:** rewriting hooks in sibling repositories, redesigning
  `wl sync`, or changing the pre-push gate are out of scope; record as linked
  follow-up items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked in this intake: the seed brief, the
reproduction transcript from the consolidated duplicate, and repository
inspection supplied enough detail to draft an unambiguous brief.

Research performed (evidence links):

- Q (self-resolved): "Does the repository already contain the post-pull
  script?" — Answer: **yes**, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is committed
  (514 bytes) but unreferenced by the wrappers. Evidence: `rg worklog-post-pull`;
  file contents.
- Q (self-resolved): "Why does the failure not appear on this host?" — Answer:
  the wrappers hard-code `/home/rgardler`, and on this host the
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` install (`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP`) provides that exact
  path as a symlink to the repo script, so checkout succeeds and the defect is
  latent. Removing the symlink for one command reproduces `rc=127`; changing
  `$HOME` alone does not, because the path is absolute. Evidence:
  `mv …/worklog-post-pull …; git worktree add …; mv back` (verified during
  intake), `ls -la ~/.config/pi/.githooks`.
- Q (self-resolved): "Is there a precedent implementation?" — Answer: **yes**,
  `ContextHub` and `AI_Hell` ship self-contained post-checkout hooks with
  `*tmp-worktree-*` and linked-worktree guards. Evidence: sibling `.githooks/`
  contents (`ContentCreator` not present on this host).
- Q (self-resolved): "Is the defect already tested?" — Answer: **no**.
  `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` tests the installer with synthetic
  hooks; nothing asserts the committed wrappers. Evidence: `rg` over `tests/`.
- Duplicate check performed: `wl search "post-pull hook"` / `"worklog hook"`
  found `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` (same defect), closed as a duplicate of this item;
  no other overlapping open or completed item found.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6** – SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing central script (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) (completed)
- **SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP** – Chore: install central wl post-pull hook (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing (completed)
- **SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K** – GIT_DIR evidence: trace non-destructive env propagation path (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: aborting, absent, absolute, acceptance, acs (+344 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, absolute, acceptance, acs, actual (+314 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: aborting, absent, absolute, actual, add (+294 more)
## Plan (2026-10-27)

**Decision: single leaf item — no child decomposition.** The change is one
atomic fix to a small, tightly-coupled hook contract (three wrappers + the
script they exec + installer wiring + docs) estimated **Small / Medium**
(5.42h expected). Splitting it into child items would leave intermediate
commits with a half-portable hook chain and a red suite — the committed suite
must be green at every commit — so the work is implemented as one vertical
slice that cuts through hooks, installer, tests and docs.

Rationale recorded per the plan skill's step 5 (phasing not required for an
item of this size; documented rather than silently skipped).

**Duplicate check:** `wl search "post-pull hook" | "worklog hook" |
"githooks portability" | "worktree add 127"` found no open item covering these
ACs. `SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6` is the already-closed duplicate of this item;
`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` (completed) installed the central symlink;
`SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1` (open) is precedent for the *local-then-global
resolution* pattern in the pre-push hook and stays a separate item.

### Implementation order (test-first; suite green at each commit)

1. **Tests first** — add `tests/test_githooks_portability.py`, hermetic and
   offline, covering:
   - (a) static: no committed wrapper contains `/home/<user>` or another
     machine-specific absolute path (guards AC1);
   - (b) temp repository built from the committed `.githooks/` with
     `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a sandboxed `$HOME` with no `.config/pi`, and
     a stub `wl` on `PATH` → `git worktree add --detach` exits 0, prints no
     `exec: ... not found`, and the repo-relative
     `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` is the script that ran (marker file);
   - (c) same setup with `worklog-post-pull` removed → `rc=0`, exactly one
     stderr notice naming both attempted locations, stub `wl` never invoked;
   - (d) `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` bypasses the sync;
   - (e) recursion guards: `PWD` containing `tmp-worktree-`, and a linked
     worktree (`--git-dir` ≠ `--git-common-dir`), both exit before `wl sync`.
2. **Rewrite the three wrappers** (`.githooks/post-checkout`, `post-merge`,
   `post-rewrite`) to resolve `worklog-post-pull` as: repo-relative
   (`<toplevel>/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, falling back to
   `dirname "$0"/worklog-post-pull`) → `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/...` →
   one-line stderr notice + `exit 0`. Test for existence/executability before
   `exec` so a missing script can never produce 127. Keep the
   `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1` marker (no version bump: `install_pi.sh`
   detects wiring by content, and the sibling projects use v1 markers).
   *Commit A: tests + wrappers.*
3. **Add recursion guards** to `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`: skip
   `*tmp-worktree-*` paths and linked worktrees before the `wl sync` call,
   mirroring the ContextHub/AI_Hell copies; keep the
   `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` bypass first.
4. **Update `scripts/install_pi.sh`**: the fail-open portability warning must
   now fire only for *legacy/foreign* wrappers (no repo-relative resolution and
   no reference to `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`), and must no
   longer warn about this repository's fixed wrappers; refresh the explanatory
   comment block. *Commit B: guards + installer.*
5. **Docs**: replace the "Portability caveat (SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX)" paragraph
   in `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` with the resolution order, the no-op
   behaviour and the bypass variables. Touch
   `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` only if the installer warning
   contract changed. *Commit C: docs.*
6. **Verify**: changed-scope tests, then the full suite via `/skill:test`
   (AC6); capture AC3 evidence (see below). *Commit D only if fix-ups are
   needed.*

### AC → verification map

| AC | Proven by |
|----|-----------|
| No hard-coded per-user path | static scan (test 1a) + resolution/`exit 0` behaviour in tests 1b/1c |
| Regression test proves `git worktree add` succeeds | tests 1a, 1b, 1c |
| `wl sync` completes its push step without the central install | see *AC3 evidence* note |
| Hooks cannot recurse | test 1e |
| Docs updated | review diff of `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, comment blocks and `install_pi.sh` |
| Full suite passes | `/skill:test` full scope before the dev push |

**AC3 evidence note.** No automated test may perform a real sync (risk noted

# Intake Brief — Drive epic children in interactive Herdr panes

## Problem statement

`implement.py drive <parent>` (`phase_drive`, SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9) runs each
child's fresh Pi session as a **headless subprocess**:

```
pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve --no-extensions
```

with `capture_output=True`. The operator therefore has:

- no view of the child session while it runs (only the parent's own progress
  lines and `wait_for_job` heartbeats);
- no ability to watch the agent work, scroll its transcript, or intervene when
  it stalls, hits an approval/question boundary, or loops;
- no evidence after a failure beyond a 5-line `_tail_lines(...)` summary of
  captured stderr/stdout;
- no per-child terminal artefact to point at during review.

An operator running an epic in Herdr already watches a grid of interactive
`π` TUI panes for other work. Drive should produce the same kind of pane —
one interactive Pi TUI session per child, opened as a sibling pane in the
caller's tab — so the epic runs *visibly*.

A headless-in-a-pane variant (option A: `pane split` + `pane run` +
exit-sentinel) was evaluated and rejected as insufficient: it shows log text,
not a browsable/typeable Pi TUI session, and offers no session-level state.

## Users

- **Operator / producer driving an epic from a Herdr-managed Pi session.**
  - *User story:* "As an operator, when I run `implement.py drive <epic>`, I
    want each child implemented in its own interactive Pi TUI pane inside the
    tab I invoked from, so I can watch progress, scroll the full transcript,
    and step in if a child stalls — without leaving my own session."
- **Reviewer / auditor.** *User story:* "As a reviewer, I want each child's
  session transcript to still be inspectable after drive finishes, so I can
  check what the agent actually did."

## Goal

`implement.py drive <parent>` opens **each** child's implementation session as
an interactive Pi TUI agent in a new pane split from the calling pane (same
tab), drives that pane's lifecycle to completion, and continues the existing
serial/blocking-order/parent-last loop — preserving session isolation,
worktree isolation, error isolation, and the recursion guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Pane-per-child in the caller's tab.** For each startable child, drive
   runs `herdr pane split` from the invoking pane (no `tab create`, no
   `workspace create`) with `--cwd <child worktree>` and returns the new pane
   id from `.result.pane.pane_id`; the child Pi TUI is started in that pane via
   `herdr agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> -- --approve
   --no-extensions` and prompted with `/skill:implement <child_id>` via
   `herdr agent prompt ... --wait`. Verified by a test that asserts the herdr
   CLI invocations (split/prompt/wait/close) and asserts no tab/workspace
   creation call is made.
2. **Driver waits on session state, not process exit.** Completion of a child
   is determined by (a) `herdr agent wait <name> --until done|blocked` for the
   pane-side signal and (b) the existing `phase_parent` re-read of the work
   item's stage as the authoritative signal. Drive never assumes an
   interactive agent process exits when the work item completes. Tests cover
   the `done`, `blocked`, and timeout transitions.
3. **Blocked children are reported, not silently abandoned.** When an agent
   reports `blocked` (approval/question UI), drive stops the chain, records the
   child id and the pane id in the JSON report (`blocked_child`,
   `blocked_pane`), leaves the pane open for the operator, and emits actionable
   text naming the pane. Tested with a fake herdr runner.
4. **No orphaned sessions:** a pane created by drive is either (a) closed once
   its child reaches a terminal stage and the child's session was clean, or
   (b) explicitly retained and reported (blocked/failed) — never leaked
   silently. Unit tests assert a close call per successful child and no close
   call for blocked/failed children.
5. **Opt-in with fail-open fallback.** Pane driving activates only when
   Herdr is detected (`HERDR_ENV=1` and a resolvable herdr binary) **and** the
   operator opted in (`--pane-sessions`, or `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_PANE_SESSIONS=1`).
   Otherwise the existing `_default_session_spawner` headless path is used
   unchanged. Tests cover herdr-absent, opt-out, and herdr-present paths.
6. **Environment isolation is preserved for pane children.** The child process
   receives `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1`, `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH=<worktree>`,
   and does **not** inherit `PI_SESSION_ID` / `PI_SESSION_FILE` from the
   driving session (assert the constructed env / pane-split `--env` args and
   the `env -u` prefix). Recursion guard and per-child worktree enforcement
   continue to work inside the pane.
7. **Timeouts and iteration bounds are enforced across the new transport.**
   `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_CHILD_TIMEOUT` (and the existing per-child session bound
   `--max-child-sessions`) still bound the wait; a timeout closes the pane,
   records `reason`, and stops the chain as today. Tested with a fake clock /
   fake herdr wait returning `timeout`.
8. **Focus behaviour.** Default is `--no-focus` so the caller's focus is
   unchanged; an explicit `--focus` variant switches to each new child pane.
   Assert the flag passed to `pane split` in both modes.
9. **Report parity.** Human and `--json` reports keep the existing shape and
   gain `pane_id` per driven child plus `transport: "pane" | "headless"`; the
   final summary lists panes retained for inspection. Tests assert the new
   fields and that existing fields are unchanged (no breaking change for
   consumers of the drive report).
10. **Docs.** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (drive section) and
    `skill/implement/SKILL.md` Step 6.1 document: pane-per-child behaviour, the
    opt-in flag/env var, focus behaviour, blocked-child handling (which pane to
    look at, and that it is intentionally left open), and the headless fallback
    for non-Herdr/automated callers.
11. **Build, tests, and full suite.** Changed-scope tests pass before commit;
    the dev-push full-suite gate is green.

## Design sketch (non-binding)

- Add `_pane_session_spawner(child_id, worktree_path, timeout, env, verbose)`
  next to `_default_session_spawner`, returning the same
  `{"success", "returncode", "reason"}` shape plus `pane_id`.
- Extract herdr CLI calls into a small injectable helper (reuse the fail-open
  style of `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`; do not duplicate its `HERDR_BIN_PATH`
  resolution logic — reuse or import it) so tests fake the CLI boundary with
  no live Herdr.
- In `phase_drive`, select the spawner by transport: existing injection point
  (`spawn_session`) already allows tests to bypass either; the CLI path chooses
  pane vs headless from the opt-in + detection check.
- Agent naming: `drive-<child-id-lowercased>` (herdr names must match
  `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`, unique among live agents) — truncation/validation
  must be tested.
- Pane labelling: on completion/failure, set the pane title via the existing
  `herdr_pane.update_pane_title(status, pane_id=...)` helper so the retained
  pane carries its verdict.

## Constraints

- Do not change the session-per-child rule (SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52), worktree
  isolation, dependency ordering, or parent-advanced-last semantics — all live
  above the spawner.
- Do not change `_default_session_spawner` behaviour for automated callers
  (downtime worker, audit dispatch, CI): headless `pi -p` must remain the
  default outside Herdr.
- No edits to the repo-external Herdr agent skill or the installed
  `~/.pi/agent/extensions/` files (herdr-managed).
- `herdr agent start` requires the pane to be at an interactive shell prompt;
  the implementation must handle `agent_not_ready` (retry within the existing
  timeout or fail with a reported reason), not crash.
- Herdr CLI failures must be fail-open at the boundary (recorded reason,
  chain stops cleanly) — never leave the epic in an unrecoverable state.

## Risks & mitigations

- **Loss of the process-exit completion signal.** An interactive TUI session
  does not exit when the work item completes, so completion must come from
  wl stage + `agent wait`. *Mitigation:* AC 2 makes `phase_parent` the
  authority (it already is) and `agent wait` only a fast-path; covered by tests.
- **Pane/session leakage.** Panes and interactive agents persist after drive
  ends. *Mitigation:* AC 4 explicit close-or-report rule, plus pane-title
  verdict marking for retained panes.
- **Serial drive + visible panes can be noisy.** One pane open at a time,
  closed on success. *Mitigation:* documented; failure/blocked panes retained
  deliberately.
- **Herdr API drift** (JSON shapes, kind list, name rules). *Mitigation:*
  single injected helper for CLI calls; parse ids defensively; fail open.
- **Approval prompts could block an unattended epic.** *Mitigation:* start
  with `--approve` and treat `blocked` as an explicit, reported stop (AC 3).

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive`, `phase_parent`,
  `_child_session_env`, `_default_session_spawner`, `_resolve_child_session_timeout`,
  `_resolve_pi_bin`, `_emit_phase_report`; `--max-child-sessions` and
  `--child-timeout` CLI flags; `spawn_session` injection point.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — deterministic orchestration tests with
  `ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner`; `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
  — spawer/env tests.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — fail-open Herdr CLI helper (`HERDR_BIN_PATH`,
  `pane list`/`pane rename`, status prefix/truncation, `update_pane_title`).
- Herdr CLI surface (verified against the installed binary): `pane split
  --current --direction right|down --cwd --env --no-focus`, `pane run`,
  `pane wait-output`, `pane read`, `pane close`, `pane rename`,
  `agent start <name> --kind pi --pane <id> [-- args]`, `agent prompt
  <target> <text> --wait [--until] [--timeout]`, `agent wait`, `agent get`,
  `agent list`, `agent read`. Caller context env: `HERDR_ENV`,
  `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`.

## Appendix: decisions from the discovery conversation

- Transport choice: **option B** (interactive Pi TUI agent in a pane) over
  option A (headless `pi -p` run in a pane, exit-sentinel + `pane read`).
  Rationale recorded: option A shows log text only; B gives a browsable,
  typeable session and Herdr's lifecycle states, at the cost of replacing the
  process-exit completion signal with wl-stage + `agent wait` (AC 2).
- Opt-in rather than default: automated callers (downtime worker, audit
  dispatch, CI) have no Herdr and must keep the headless path (AC 5).
- Forked-decision for planning: whether to factor the herdr CLI boundary into a
  shared module (`skill/shared/`) or keep it local to `implement.py`; prefer
  reuse of `herdr_pane.py`'s resolution/fail-open conventions either way.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9** — implement skill: drive all epic children to
  completion (fresh session per child) — the headless drive this item extends.
- **SA-0MUWBHEEF002A6BO** — When running implement on a parent item implement
  all children — original one-invocation drive requirement.
- **SA-0MTLCCIPU0050Q52** — When implementing an epic start a new session for
  each child — session isolation rule that must be preserved.
- **SA-0MVDQF3VW002PKCA** — User-visible progress feedback during long-running
  waits — related observability work for drive runs.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion — reuse `herdr_pane.update_pane_title` for retained panes.

# `implement.py parent`/`drive` start children whose status is `blocked` — re-validate the block before starting or skipping

Discovered-from: **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6** (tce-main-street) — producer decision Q3 (2026-10-29): *"yes, though it should first check that the block is still valid"*.

## Goal

As an implement agent running an epic, I need `implement.py parent`/`drive` to never start a child that is deliberately `blocked` unless the block no longer holds, so a verification child is not implemented against a prerequisite that has not landed and I am not asked to fabricate its evidence.

## Problem statement

`phase_parent()` classifies children with `_classify_child()` (`implement/scripts/implement.py:874`): terminal → `skip-terminal`, `in-progress` → `skip-in-progress`, **everything else → `implement`**. Status `blocked` therefore falls through to `implement`.

Blocker awareness exists but does not gate the start:

- `_in_chain_blockers()` only considers blockers that are **themselves children of the same parent** (`implement.py:5920-5975`), so a child blocked on anything outside the parent's children set is startable.
- `external_blockers` is populated from outbound `wl dep` edges only (`implement.py:5771-5790`) and is reported as a "coordination note". It is `[]` when the block is recorded in prose instead of as a dependency edge — which is how cross-project blocks are written (`**Blocked by (SorraAgents):** SA-…` in the child description).

**Live evidence (this item's origin):** on 2026-10-29 `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` started child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` — status `blocked`, unblock condition "`SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2` is in `dev`/`in_review`", which was still `open`/`intake_complete` — created a worktree and reported `external_blockers: []`. The child had to be aborted (`implement.py abort`, worktree removed) to avoid producing unverifiable AC evidence.

The inverse failure matters too: a **stale** block must not strand a child forever. Once the blocker lands, the child must become startable again (or its status refreshed) rather than being skipped silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A child whose `status` is `blocked` is never started while its block still holds: `_classify_child()` (or the caller) yields a distinct `skip-blocked` outcome, and the child is reported in `children_processed` with its blocking ids — not started, not `skipped-in-progress`.
- [ ] **Re-validation of dependency-edge blocks:** for a `blocked` child the outbound `wl dep list` edges are resolved; the block is **stale** iff every blocker is terminal (`completed`/`done`/`in_review`) or soft-deleted, in which case the child is startable again (and the stale block is named in the report/log). Any non-terminal blocker holds the block.
- [ ] **Re-validation of cross-project and prose blocks:** blocker IDs declared in the child description's `Blocked by …` line (and/or a machine-readable `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented) are collected and surfaced in `external_blockers`; an unresolvable cross-project id holds the block and is reported with an actionable message (id + where to check it), never silently ignored and never silently startable.
- [ ] A block that cannot be validated (no dep edges, no parseable blocker line, unknown status) is treated as **holding** and reported as unvalidated — it must not default to startable.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: (a) `blocked` + open external blocker → not started, reported with ids; (b) `blocked` + blocker now terminal → stale block detected and child started; (c) `blocked` + no resolvable blocker → not started, message names the unresolved id; (d) `drive` propagates the same classification/report fields; (e) existing in-chain sibling ordering, cycles and terminal/in-progress behaviour unchanged (regression cases).
- [ ] Live evidence recorded on this item: re-running `implement.py parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (three `blocked` verification children) starts nothing and reports all three with their `SA-…` blockers.
- [ ] `implement/SKILL.md` "Guards" list gains the blocked-child re-validation rule (stale blocks are re-evaluated, not honoured forever), and the parent-recursion section documents the new report vocabulary.
- [ ] Node and pytest suites green for the changed framework code (run through the test skill / finish gate, never an ad-hoc runner).

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the existing guards: dependency order, cycle fail-fast, "never re-implement terminal children", "never clobber another agent's `in_progress` claim", and `--finalise-stranded` semantics stay as they are.
- No change to `implement.py start`/`finish` single-item behaviour; this is the parent/`drive` fan-out classification only.
- Cross-project resolution must stay fail-open in the sense that an unresolvable id reports clearly and does not crash the phase — it just holds the block.
- Prose parsing must not become the only mechanism: prefer declared dependency edges, and keep the prose path narrowly scoped to an explicit `Blocked by` line.

## Key Files

- `implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child()`, `phase_parent()` (child classification, `_in_chain_blockers`), `phase_drive()` (report propagation), `wl_dep_blockers()`.
- `implement/scripts/tests/` (or the repo's existing implement test location) — new unit tests for the classification matrix.
- `implement/SKILL.md` — Guards + parent recursion report vocabulary.
- Reference cases: `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` children `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`, `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO`, `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR`, `MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` (all `blocked`, blockers in prose).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`, `SA-0MVL7YOMJ006UMDO`, `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` — the three blockers of the origin item's verification children.
- `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T` — introduced `external_blockers` as coordination notes; this item makes them gate the start.

---

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-10-30)

**Headline:** Split the fix into a test-first contract item, three vertical
behaviour slices (classification → prose/cross-project blockers → drive
reporting), a docs item and a live-evidence item, all under this parent, with
every parent AC mapped to a child.

### Child work items (test-first, dependency order)

| # | Id | Title | Type | Effort/Risk |
|---|----|-------|------|-------------|
| C1 | `SA-0MVUTD3IX004E03C` | Tests: blocked-child classification matrix for parent/drive | task | M / Medium |
| C2 | `SA-0MVUTD408005OFNW` | phase_parent: classify a still-blocked child as `skip-blocked` (dep-edge re-validation) | feature | M / Medium |
| C3 | `SA-0MVUTD4HS000O6AB` | Prose `Blocked by` and cross-project blockers hold a blocked child | feature | M / Medium |
| C4 | `SA-0MVUTD4ZD006O4N5` | phase_drive: propagate `skip-blocked` classification and blocker ids | feature | S / Low |
| C5 | `SA-0MVUTD5GQ004V6UO` | Docs: `implement/SKILL.md` guards + parent-recursion report vocabulary | docs | XS / Low |
| C6 | `SA-0MVUTD5YF001PLOF` | Live evidence: `parent MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` starts no blocked child | task | S / Medium |

Dependency edges (all wired with `wl dep add`):

```
C1 (tests, no blockers)
 └─ C2 ─┬─ C3 ─┬─ C4 ─┬─ C5 (docs)
        │      │      └─ C6 (live evidence)
        └──────┴────────┘
```

Ordering rationale: C1 writes the red contract first (parent AC 5); C2 lands
the dep-edge verdict (AC 1, 2, 4-dep-path); C3 adds the prose/cross-project
path (AC 3, 4-prose-path) and makes the fail-closed default actionable; C4
propagates the verdict through `drive` (AC 1 "reported in `children_processed`"
on the drive path); C5 documents the shipped vocabulary (AC 7); C6 produces the
live evidence (AC 6). Each slice is end-to-end: code + tests + the finish gate.

### Parent AC → child coverage

| Parent AC | Covered by |
|---|---|
| AC1 `skip-blocked` distinct outcome, reported in `children_processed` with blocking ids | C2 (classification + report), C4 (drive propagation), C1(a) |
| AC2 dep-edge re-validation, stale iff every blocker terminal/soft-deleted | C2, C1(b) |
| AC3 prose `Blocked by` / cross-project ids surfaced in `external_blockers`; unresolvable holds with an actionable message | C3, C1(c) |
| AC4 unvalidatable block holds and is reported unvalidated | C2 (no dep edges), C3 (no parseable line) |
| AC5 unit tests (a)–(e) | C1 |
| AC6 live evidence on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` | C6 |
| AC7 `implement/SKILL.md` Guards + report vocabulary | C5 |
| AC8 node + pytest suites green through the test skill / finish gate | every child's finish gate; stated explicitly in C1 and C2 |

### Assumptions (recorded, not invented requirements)

- **A1 — test location.** The Key Files section above predicted
  `implement/scripts/tests/`; the repo's existing implement tests live in
  `tests/test_implement_*.py` at the repo root, so C1 creates
  `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` there.
- **A2 — prose only, no schema change.** AC3's "and/or a machine-readable
  `externalBlockers` field, whichever is implemented" is satisfied by parsing
  the explicit `Blocked by …` line plus declared dependency edges; no `wl`
  schema change (wl is a separate ContextHub-owned CLI).
- **A3 — cross-project ids are resolvable in principle.** `implement.py`
  already routes `wl` calls through
  `shared/status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`, whose prefix-to-sibling scan
  maps an id prefix to its owning project's worklog. Verified on 2026-10-30:
  from `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street`, prefix `SA` resolves to
  `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog` and `MS` to the tce worklog.
  Whether C3 *uses* that to detect a landed cross-project blocker is Q3 below.
- **A4 — one existing test encodes the superseded contract.**
  `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py::TestParentDependencyOrder::test_external_blocker_reported_not_started_early`
  asserts that a `blocked` child with an out-of-chain blocker **is started**
  ("coordination notes" per `SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T`). This item deliberately
  supersedes that behaviour; C1 updates and renames the test rather than
  leaving two contradictory contracts.
- **A5 — legacy helper kept.** `_next_child_to_implement()` has no production
  call site (only `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`); C2 keeps it
  consistent with the new rule instead of deleting it (dead code is reported,
  not removed, in a bug-fix slice).
- **A6 — the live-evidence run can start something.** The origin epic's AC1
  child `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` is `open` (not `blocked`) with
  `assignee: Map` + tag `do-not-delegate`; `phase_parent` honours neither
  (that is `SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876`, itself `blocked`). See Q1.
- **A7 — `blocked` status writes are unreliable.** `WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82`
  (ContextHub) records `wl update --status blocked` reporting success while the
  stored status reverted to `open`; the classification must therefore never
  depend on the framework being able to *write* `blocked`.

### Plan: changelog

# `phase_parent`: classify a still-blocked child as `skip-blocked` (dep-edge re-validation)

Parent: **SA-0MVTUFL0U0000NV2**. Test-first sibling: **C1** (blocked-child classification matrix).

## Goal

As an implement agent running an epic, I need `implement.py parent` to never
start a child whose `status` is `blocked` while its block still holds, and to
re-evaluate (not honour forever) a **stale** block, so a verification child is
never implemented against a prerequisite that has not landed and a landed
prerequisite never strands its dependent.

## Context

- `_classify_child()` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, ~line 1127)
  returns `implement` for `status: blocked`. Precedence today:
  terminal → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `implement`.
- `phase_parent()` (~line 6609) builds `classifications` with
  `action`/`external_blockers` and gates the start only on **in-chain**
  blockers (`_in_chain_blockers`, blockers that are themselves children of the
  same parent, ~line 6787). `_next_child_to_implement()` (~line 1227) is a
  second, legacy classification path kept consistent by tests.
- `wl dep list <id> --json` → `outbound` entries with `id` and `status`
  (`wl_dep_blockers`, ~line 565).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A `blocked` child whose block still holds yields a **distinct** classification (`skip-blocked`, i.e. `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED`) from `_classify_child()` (or its caller); it is never `implement`, `skip-in-progress` or `skipped-terminal`. Precedence is explicit and documented: `skip-terminal` → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `skip-blocked` → `implement`.
- [ ] **Dep-edge re-validation:** for a `blocked` child the outbound `wl dep list` edges are resolved; the block is **stale** iff every blocker is terminal (`completed`/`done`/`in_review`, reusing `_is_terminal_status` / soft-delete semantics) — in which case the child is startable again and the stale block is named in the report (a `stale_blocks` entry, and a log/comment line naming the blocker ids). Any **non-terminal** blocker holds the block.
- [ ] `children_processed` entries for a held child carry `action: "skip-blocked"`, the child id, its status and `blocking_ids` (the ids that hold it); the report also lists them in `blocked_children` so `phase_drive`'s existing propagation keeps working.
- [ ] A block that cannot be validated (no dep edges, no parseable blocker line, unknown status) is treated as **holding** and reported as unvalidated (`unvalidated_blocks`) — it must not default to startable. (The prose/cross-project resolution that makes such a child actionable lands in C3; until then the fail-closed behaviour is the correct default.)
- [ ] A `blocked` child with at least one terminal blocker **and** one non-terminal blocker still holds (the non-terminal one wins); a `blocked` child whose blockers are all soft-deleted is stale/startable.
- [ ] `_next_child_to_implement()` (legacy helper, still covered by `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py`) applies the same rule so the two classification paths cannot diverge; it is kept, not deleted.
- [ ] Unchanged: dependency order, cycle fail-fast, terminal children never re-implemented, `skipped-held` precedence, `skip-in-progress` never clobbering another agent's claim, `--finalise-stranded` semantics, and single-item `start`/`finish` behaviour.
- [ ] The C1 tests for cases (a), (b) and (e) are green; the changed-scope suite is green through the finish gate (`/skill:test`) and the full pytest + node suite is green at the dev-push gate (parent AC 8).

## Minimal implementation sketch

- Add `ACTION_SKIP_BLOCKED = "skip-blocked"` beside `ACTION_SKIPPED_HELD` (~line 213).
- New helper, e.g. `_blocked_child_state(child, blockers) -> {"action", "blocking_ids", "stale_ids", "unvalidated"}`, called from `_classify_child`'s callers (`phase_parent`, `_next_child_to_implement`) with the child's outbound edges — `_classify_child` itself has no edge data, so either widen its signature with an optional `blockers` argument (defaulting to `None` → unvalidated/fail-closed) or keep the status test in `_classify_child` and resolve the blocked verdict in the callers. Prefer the smallest change that keeps both call sites consistent.
- Extend the `classifications`/`child_results` entries and the "no startable child" message to name the blockers.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken existing guards; do not change `start`/`finish` single-item behaviour.
- Prefer declared dependency edges over prose; no `wl` schema change, no `gh`/network calls.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_classify_child` (~1127), `_next_child_to_implement` (~1227), `phase_parent` (~6609, incl. `_in_chain_blockers` ~6787), `wl_dep_blockers` (~565), `TERMINAL_STATUSES`/`_is_terminal_status` (~1082).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_blocked_child.py` — C1's matrix (red to green).
- `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` — existing parent suite that must stay green.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_dependency.py` — existing dependency-order suite that must stay green.

# GitHub closes the idle SSH connection during the pre-push full-suite gate

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** — this is the concrete root cause behind one of the
"transient push-transport closes" that item asks us to retry. Retrying does not
help on its own: the connection is dropped with a *deterministic* trigger
(SSH idling for the duration of the suite), so every attempt fails the same way
and the agent loops, burning a full suite run each time.

## Problem

`.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full` **after** `git` has
established the SSH connection to `github.com` and **before** the ref update.
The hook produces no SSH traffic for the whole run (measured 11 min warm, 35 min
cold on this host), so the remote closes the idle connection:

```
pre-push: full-suite gate for dev/main push — running run_tests.py --scope full ...
Connection to github.com closed by remote host.
pre-push: full suite green (cached runs make repeat pushes cheap)
pre-push: mirrored gate cache entry 96dd15da... into .worklog/cache
```

The gate reports **green**, the cache entries are mirrored — and the push never
lands: `git push` exits without updating the ref and `origin/dev` is unchanged.
Observed 2026-10-31 on two consecutive attempts from
`wl-LP-0MVWIA33O004RKP7-…` in `llm-manager`; `~/.ssh/config` sets no
`ServerAliveInterval`/`TCPKeepAlive`.

Impact:

- A green full-suite run is discarded, so the most expensive part of the push is
  paid repeatedly; because each retry rebases onto a moved `dev`, the tree
  changes and the suite cache misses, so retries are *cold*.
- The output reads as success ("full suite green") while the push silently did
  not happen — the misleading signal is arguably worse than a hard failure.

## Workaround that worked (not a fix)

```bash
GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20 -o TCPKeepAlive=yes" \
  WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dev
# -> d925d89d..877a6512  HEAD -> dev
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- A dev push whose pre-push gate runs longer than the remote's idle timeout
      succeeds, with no manual `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` override by the agent.
- Keepalives are configured in a way that survives a fresh clone/worktree
      (e.g. set by the hook or by `implement.py`'s push, not only in one
      operator's `~/.ssh/config`).
- When the ref update is still lost after a green suite, the push reports a
      distinct, loud failure (not "full suite green" followed by silence), and
      distinguishes "suite red" from "transport lost".
- A regression test covers the transport-loss path (simulated closed
      connection) and asserts the distinct failure classification.

## Notes

- `SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3` / `SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN` (push must run from the worktree)
  is a separate defect; both were hit in the same session. This item is only the
  transport side.
- Related: `~/.ssh/config` on the multi-agent host currently has no
  `ServerAlive*` settings at all.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVZQVDUY0011DQD** – tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py is not hermetic: fails under the pre-push hook's exported GIT_DIR, blocking dev pushes (open)
- **SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5** – Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs: transient SSH auth failures and push races make leaf finish fail after the work has landed (open)
- **SA-0MUUIPK2P008Y16G** – Verify full test suite green and sync on epic completion (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: acceptance, agent, asks, attempt, attempts (+134 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: agent, asks, asserts, attempt, attempts (+129 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptance, agent, asks, asserts, attempt (+126 more)

## Problem statement

Tests exercising `implement.py`'s main-checkout lock-wait path inherit the ambient
`IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` environment variables
and hang for hours instead of refusing immediately (the default `0` = fail-fast).

### Reproduction (verified 2026-11-08 on `dev`)

```
IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT=25 python3 -m pytest \
  skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py::test_finish_refuses_when_lock_held_by_other_finish
# 1 passed in 25.18s   ← the whole ambient timeout is slept, then it refuses
```

The same test normally completes in ~0.05 s. With
`IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT=10800` (the value an agent exports to wait out a
concurrent `finish`) the single test blocks for three hours.

### Mechanism

`test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py::test_finish_refuses_when_lock_held_by_other_finish`
takes the real main-checkout `flock` itself, then calls `phase_finish`, which calls
`_finish_lock_timeout()` → `_resolve_lock_timeout(ENV_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT, 0.0)` →
`os.environ.get(...)`. `RepoLock.acquire` then honours that ambient value and retries
in `time.sleep(RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS)` steps until the deadline — but the lock it is
waiting for is held by the test's own fd, released only in the test's `finally` block.
The test therefore cannot succeed early: it burns the inherited timeout in full.

## Users

- **Agent sessions** running `implement.py finish` that export a high lock timeout to
  wait for a real concurrent finish. A child test suite then hangs for hours on a
  lock-refusal test, masking the real result.
- **CI jobs** and any automated runner that sets these env vars for real `finish` calls.

## Audit findings (2026-11-08)

Completed as part of planning so implementation does not repeat it:

- `skill/implement/tests/` contains **no** test that names either lock-timeout
  variable, so no test sets one deliberately as a test input (confirms the
  "Assumption" below).
- Only two lock-wait timeouts are read from the environment by `implement.py`:
  `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (`_finish_lock_timeout()`) and
  `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (`_start_lock_timeout()`), both through
  `_resolve_lock_timeout()`. These are the complete neutralisation set.
- `test_phase_start_child_lock.py` and `test_drive_child_lock.py` exercise child
  locks (`IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_DIR`, already isolated by
  `isolated_implement_child_lock_store`) and patch `_sync_parent_branch`; they do
  not contend the main-checkout lock, so they do not sleep on the ambient value.
- `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_CHILD_TIMEOUT` is a per-child *session* timeout, not a lock wait,
  and no test reads it — out of scope.
- `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` is the test-slot pool bound owned by
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, not `implement.py`; the implement tests stub
  `run_gate_suite`, so it is unreachable from `skill/implement/tests/` and out of
  scope given the "changes stay within `skill/implement/tests/`" constraint.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `pytest skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` passes in under 5 seconds with `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT=10800` and `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT=600` exported.
- An autouse fixture in `skill/implement/tests/conftest.py` neutralises `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` and `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` for every test in the package, mirroring the existing `_no_ambient_git_index_file` fixture pattern; a test asserts the fixture's effect (both variables absent, or `"0"`, while it is active).
- The regression test `test_finish_refuses_when_lock_held_by_other_finish` completes without sleeping — asserted via elapsed time < 5 seconds (or equivalent clock-patch assertion) with the ambient variables exported.
- The audit above is reflected in the change: no other test in `skill/implement/tests/` reaches `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and this is stated in a code comment so it need not be re-derived.
- `pytest skill/implement/tests/` passes, and the full project test suite passes with the changes.

## Impact

Agents and CI jobs that export lock-wait timeouts for their own `finish` calls no
longer poison test suites with multi-hour hangs on lock-refusal tests.

## Constraints

- The fix must be additive — no behavioural change to production code.
- Follow the existing `conftest.py` autouse-fixture pattern for environment
  neutralisation.
- Changes stay within `skill/implement/tests/`.

## Existing state

- `_resolve_lock_timeout()` (line ~2908 of `implement.py`) reads from `os.environ` with
  no neutralisation.
- `conftest.py` already neutralises `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_DIR` via
  autouse fixtures.
- `test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` calls `phase_finish` which calls
  `_finish_lock_timeout()` — inheriting the ambient value.
- `_sync_parent_branch_locked()` calls `_start_lock_timeout()` → the same inheritance.

## Desired change

Add an autouse fixture (or extend the existing environment-neutralising group) in
`skill/implement/tests/conftest.py` that `monkeypatch.delenv()`s
`IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` and `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` for every test,
documented with the mechanism above so the reason survives. Add the elapsed-time
assertion to the refusal regression test.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/tests/conftest.py` — add neutralising fixture
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — source of `_finish_lock_timeout()` / `_start_lock_timeout()` / `_resolve_lock_timeout()`
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock.acquire` retry loop that sleeps out the inherited timeout
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` — affected test
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_lock.py` — audited: child lock only, unaffected
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_child_lock.py` — audited: child lock only, unaffected

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: no test intentionally sets these timeout variables as test inputs.
  The variables represent caller policy, never test inputs, so neutralisation is safe.
  (Where a test *does* need a specific value, it sets it explicitly within the test
  body, after the fixture has run.) Verified by the audit above.
- **Scope-creep risk**: `test_drive_child_lock.py` and other integration tests that
  spawn subprocesses inherit the fixture's env-hermeticity. If a subprocess *must*
  read the ambient timeout, the test should re-export it explicitly after the fixture
  runs. The audit found no such case.
- **Existing pattern**: the `_no_ambient_git_index_file` autouse fixture already
  neutralises an ambient var via `monkeypatch.delenv`. The new fixture follows the
  same pattern.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVY0G5EH000LIMB` — this item
- `SA-0MUV2UBMT008OE2E` — Test infra concurrency issue (related category)
- `SA-0MPGTWHQF005HO05` — Process cleanup (related infrastructure)

*As a producer/release operator*, I need proof that a `slot_busy` verdict means
the pool really was full for the whole wait, and *as a framework maintainer* I
need the cross-process discovery rule pinned, so "the waiter is stuck" can never
be mistaken for "retry later" (SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0).

## Context

Two gaps are unpinned today:

1. **Cross-process discovery.** A low-ceiling waiter (`max_workers=2`) cannot
   use a higher-index slot (`3`) that another process created and left free —
   the defect described in the parent item and reproduced in-process by the
   sibling test child.
2. **Genuine saturation.** `slot_busy` must keep meaning "every slot in the

## Goal

Prove, with tests, that a run's `AUDIT_RELIABILITY_SUMMARY` describes the current attempt and
that a leftover abort-recovery state file cannot short-circuit or distort a retry.

**User story:** As an operator debugging a failed audit, I want the reliability summary and the

## Context / evidence (from the parent plan investigation)

  short-circuit a retry today.

  counters and summary values (no bleed-through between runs);

## Goal

Implement the failure classification and relatedness helper functions in `audit_runner.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_classify_test_failure_scope(failure)` returns `"unit"` or `"integration"`:
   - Path convention: `tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` → `integration`
   - Everything else → `unit`
   - Unclassifiable (no path data) → `integration` (fail closed)

2. `_failure_relatedness(failure, touched_files, key_files, project_root)` returns `"affected"`, `"unrelated"`, or `"inconclusive"`:
   - Test file path ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Module imported by test file ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Changed file is shared test infrastructure (`conftest.py`, `tests/helpers/**`) → `affected`
   - No match → `inconclusive`

3. `_baseline_unrelated(failures, project_root, baseline_commit)` returns per-failure verdicts:
   - Creates scratch worktree at baseline commit (pre-change commit)
   - Runs only inconclusive failures through `paced_runner()` under `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` stand-down
   - Identical failure → `unrelated`; Pass → `affected`
   - Any baseline failure → `affected` (fail closed)
   - Any baseline error (worktree add, merge-base unresolvable, test absent) → `affected` (fail closed, no crash)
   - Never executes the main checkout; never recurses into nested suite runs

4. Scope classification and relatedness algorithm: failures are classified by path convention (`tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` ⇒ integration/end-to-end; everything else ⇒ unit; unclassifiable ⇒ integration, fail closed). Relatedness is decided by deterministic mapping first (failing test file ∈ item's changed files; a module the test imports ∈ changed files; a changed shared test-infrastructure file such as `conftest.py`/`tests/helpers/**`), then — only for inconclusive failures — by a baseline re-run of just those failures in a scratch worktree at the item's pre-change commit (fails identically ⇒ unrelated; passes ⇒ affected). Unit tests cover the pattern table, the import-mapping step, and the baseline comparison (both outcomes), with no real suite execution.

5. No real suite execution in unit tests (mock `paced_runner` / subprocess)
6. Unit tests pass (see child test items)

## Deliverables
- `_classify_test_failure_scope()` — path-pattern classifier
- `_failure_relatedness()` — deterministic mapping + import scan
- `_baseline_unrelated()` — scratch worktree baseline re-run
- Error handling: never crashes, always returns `affected` for infrastructure failures

## Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (new functions)

# Regression harness for finish commit-vs-no-op (test-first slice)

## Context

Parent SA-0MVYYL7X9008MGA1: `implement.py finish` currently finalises a work
item even when its worktree produced **no commit attributable to the item**,
reporting the ambient `dev` HEAD as if it were the item's commit. The
behaviour slices that fix this need a test harness that can distinguish
"a commit was created" from "nothing to commit": today the stub git boundary
in `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` succeeds for both,
so no test can pin the difference.

This is a **test-only** slice (red/green preparation): no production code
changes here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — The fake git boundary in the finish tests can simulate both a real commit and a clean, commit-less tree, recording whether `git commit` ran, so a test can distinguish a real commit from a no-op finish.
- AC2 — The existing OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58 regression pin (the no-diff path persists `completed`/`in_review`) remains green after the harness change.
- AC3 — A reusable helper asserts the completion-comment/report wording, so later slices can assert a commit hash is present on the commit path and absent ("no changes / no commit") on the no-op path.
- AC4 — A reusable helper builds a `_classify_child`/`phase_parent` fixture (child dict plus worktree state file) that later slices reuse, and it is exercised by at least one test against current behaviour.

## Minimal implementation

- Add an explicit outcome mode to the fake `run_cmd` stub: `commit` mode (staged diff present, `git commit` recorded as invoked) and `clean` mode (no staged diff, `git commit` never invoked).
- Add a report/comment wording helper (e.g. `assert_report_wording(report, *, commit_hash=None)`) used by later slices.
- Add child/worktree fixture helpers (child dict + `.implement_state.json` writer) reusable by the drive-classification slice.
- Keep `test_finish_no_diff_status.py` assertions unchanged apart from harness wiring.

## Key Files:

- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — harness outcome modes and the existing no-diff pin.
- `skill/implement/tests/conftest.py` — shared fixture placement where appropriate.

## Definition of done

- Changed-scope tests pass (test skill); no production file touched.
- Later slices can express "commit happened" vs "nothing to commit" without new stubbing per test.

## Impact

Test authors can deterministically simulate a commit-less finish, so the
false `in_review` regression is pinnable instead of only discovered after an
incident.
